evidence: Purdue ArcGIS feature FID 862 identifies Marriott Hall (MRRT) at 900 Mitch Daniels Blvd (the service's separate BUILDING_1 field is 1423).
Recomputed source polygon has 33 unique ring vertices and approximately 1980.4 m² area under the mandated local campus transform.
Purdue venue listing identifies Marriott Hall and the same street address; independent architect project page names Purdue as client and describes the same building.
Feature identity is cross-checked by ID, abbreviation, name, and address rather than nearest-location alone. GIS outline is not a certified survey.
Independent Blender reopen found 33/33 transformed source vertices in the evaluated mesh within 1 mm; maximum nearest-vertex error 0.000019 m.

Footprint and cardinal orientation follow the official EPSG:3857 feature using its documented inverse projection and the project’s approximate WGS84-to-campus conversion. This verifies geometric registration to that GIS source, not survey-grade position.
GIS record lists four levels; model height is 12.67 m with eave/ridge estimates of 9.6/12.6 m.
The builder and source evidence correctly label vertical dimensions estimates; ArcGIS Extrution=39 has no documented units and is not treated as a measured elevation.

Architect and Purdue photos confirm a broad red pitched roof with deep eaves, so a gable silhouette is evidence-based. The rendered roof is an irregular collection of overlapping/faceted roof planes across the GIS footprint, unlike the dominant long continuous gable seen in the reference photos; exact roof plan and height remain unverified.
The exterior reads as roughly three above-grade facade bands despite a GIS four-level attribute; the fourth level's interpretation is unresolved.

Architect and Purdue source photos show red brick, light horizontal masonry bands, vertical brick piers, upper transparent glazing, lower punched windows, deep roof eaves, and a visible glazed entrance/canopy.
Preview captures brick, light belt courses, upper glazing, lower windows, gabled red roof, overhang, entrance doors, a metal canopy, and steps.

Facade rhythm is schematic: source photos show prominent vertical piers, tall upper curtain-wall bays, a larger entrance-side covered plaza, and a more legible lobby. The preview's entrance canopy/doors are much smaller and less distinctive, and window dimensions are not measured.
Independent Blender 5.2 reopen found expected scene Building_massing_marriot_hall_7cd3eb5, collection Asset_massing_marriot_hall_7cd3eb5, one mesh, 4688 vertices, and 3344 faces.
Model has 0 modifiers, 0 linked libraries, and 0 unpacked image dependencies; the identity world matrix preserves the massing library's campus-coordinate convention.

Manifest entry matches asset ID, file, collection, scene, and one-object export. Evidence has raw feature and layer metadata, source photos/pages, architect information, project approval PDF, retrieval dates, projection/method notes, uncertainty, two previews, and a separate reopen-validation record.

findings.finding: Roof geometry needs review: the preview has large intersecting/faceted roof surfaces that create multiple apparent ridges over the irregular footprint, while the source photos primarily show a long, clear gable roof with deep eaves. The model height and roof dimensions remain estimates.

The four-level GIS attribute is not reconciled with the approximately three visible above-grade facade bands in the model/reference view. Clarify whether the extra level is below grade or whether a facade level is missing before claiming floor-count fidelity.

The principal entrance and upper glazed lobby are present in simplified form, but the real building's broad entrance-side canopy/plaza and tall glazed bays are more prominent than the model preview suggests.

The GIS footprint is an official Purdue polygon and matches the transformed mesh ring within 0.1 mm, but the service does not publish survey accuracy or a feature edit date. Height, facade bay spacing, and exact roof plan are not dimensioned in the collected sources.
The 2009 approval lists 42,500 gross square feet while the architect project page lists 35,000 square feet; neither is used to scale the source footprint, and the difference remains unexplained.

The GIS Shape__Area attribute stored in the evidence is 3,423.2, which exceeds the approximate 2,499 m² source bounding rectangle; its units/meaning are unclear, so the evaluator recomputes polygon area from the source ring and does not rely on that attribute.

source_uncertainties: Purdue GIS provides a source footprint but not certified survey accuracy; the source polygon appears to match the Marriott Hall identity and placement, but exact wall-to-GIS registration remains dependent on the source mapping.
No measured building height or roof elevations were found. GIS Extrution=39 has no documented units; modeled heights remain estimates.
The GIS level count is 4, while the exterior model depicts three above-grade facade bands; interpretation of the fourth level is unverified.
Two institutional/project sources give different building-area figures (42,500 GSF in the 2009 approval and 35,000 sf on the architect page); neither is used as footprint area.
Window bay spacing, facade material color, canopy proportions, and roof overhang are visual estimates.
This asset remains a campus-coordinate massing library; Tobin owns master integration.
